title: ‘I don’t blame any woman for being sucked in’: how the wellness industry is cynically exploiting menopause
text:
Where women see hot flushes and brain fog, pharmaceutical companies see dollar signs. But are products like lion’s mane mushrooms or even magnets for knickers really helping them? Or is it all just a big capitalist con?

 ‘Tequila?” says a woman brightly, proffering a pink plastic shot glass. It’s barely 10.30 on a Saturday morning, and my perimenopause wellness journey is not going entirely as expected. We are standing in a neon-lit London conference centre amid the hubbub of Pause Live , billed as the UK’s biggest annual women’s health and menopause event and essentially a consumer fair for those in midlife. All around me, women are sampling free squirts of menthol lotion (supposed to cool hot flushes) and paper thimblefuls of slightly grainy, sweet latte made with powdered Peruvian maca root instead of coffee.

 The tequila, it turns out, is a gift from the sponsors, with no miracle ingredients beyond alcohol. But stalls offer everything from neck creams to pelvic-floor trainers, mindfulness journals and hairpieces for disguising thinning locks, plus herbal supplements in every conceivable edible form: chocolate truffles, ginger shots, mushroom coffee. ( Fungi are big news in the menopause wellness world, often touted as an answer to brain fog. Though at best the scientific jury is still out, Ocado searches for lion’s mane mushrooms more than quadrupled after an episode of Clarkson’s Farm in which Jeremy Clarkson’s partner, Lisa Hogan, persuaded him to grow them to make supplements, claiming that “everyone who’s anyone” is on them.)
